changes.comment: BREAKING: Review: Feishu COT cards are now keyed by recipient rather than by Feishu target. Every TeamLeader and the Dispatcher owns exactly one standing anchor and at most one open card, wherever the anchor came from. A Feishu inbound becomes that anchor when the Channel submits it: the superseded open card closes as interrupted and its successor opens under the new message before Core runs. Only rejected, failed, and stopped outcomes retire the optimistic anchor; submitted, duplicate, ambiguous, and unknown-error outcomes keep it, so a duplicate delivery remains anchored while its earlier admitted turn continues. The Channel recognizes its own submitted turn from the existing caller-supplied `source_id` and hides that turn's already-visible user body once; every other producer's body displays normally. A card closes only when the runtime reports the end of its one native turn (completed closes as done; failed or interrupted closes as interrupted); that fact closes an already open card and never opens one, so it is ignored when no card is open. `teammate.turn.settled` no longer closes, reopens, or re-anchors anything. A card create or append the platform refuses abandons only that card: the standing anchor survives, and the next opening activity tries to open a card there again. A Reply is outbound only and never creates, replaces, or retires an anchor. A visible Team bind card may initialize a TeamLeader that has no standing anchor and never replaces an existing one; the Dispatcher has no installation or restart anchor. A tool result that arrives after an anchor replacement may be omitted. Anchors and cards live only in the live session's memory and are lost on restart by design, with no replay or backfill. The package's public export surface is unchanged; the target-keyed and dispatcher-scoped COT presentation modules this replaces were always internal. No transport, configuration, persisted state, or path shape changed and no rebuild is required.
